title: Brioche triangle shawl
subtitle: A top-down DK triangle with a two-colour brioche body — squishy and dramatic.
excerpt: A top-down triangular shawl in DK wool, worked in two-colour brioche stitch with a garter-tab cast-on. Each wing is brioche; the spine is a single garter column in main colour. Wingspan approximately 140 cm, centre-back depth approximately 65 cm. About 200 g each of two DK yarns in strongly contrasting values.
sourceNotes: Two-colour brioche technique is documented in Nancy Marchant, Brioche Knitting (2010). Applying two-colour brioche to a top-down triangular shawl construction is a contemporary synthesis; no single source is definitive. The top-down triangle construction follows Elizabeth Zimmermann, Knitting Without Tears (1971).

knitting.gaugeText: 20 sts × 30 rows = 10 × 10 cm in two-colour brioche on 4.5 mm needles, relaxed.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Wingspan approximately 140 cm. Centre-back depth approximately 65 cm. Relaxed (brioche is not blocked).

glossaryTerms.definition: A small strip of garter stitch worked on a few stitches, rotated and picked up to form the centre-back starting point of a top-down triangle shawl.
Knit the next stitch together with its paired yarn-over from the previous row. In two-colour brioche, worked with the colour not used on the previous pass.
Slip the next stitch purlwise with yarn over the needle. Creates the paired stitch worked as brk or brp on the following pass.

content.text: A top-down triangular shawl in DK wool worked in two-colour brioche stitch with a single MC garter spine column at the centre back, started with a
garter tab
. Wingspan approximately 140 cm, depth approximately 65 cm.

Two-colour brioche is rated ADVANCED here because of the multi-colour pass management on a shaped piece: the wings increase while maintaining the strict colour alternation of brioche. The fabric is not blocked, since wet-blocking brioche flattens its characteristic three-dimensional rib. Budget about 200 g (about 440 m / 480 yards) each of two DK yarns in contrasting values.
What you need

items.name: Colour A (main)
items.qty: About 200 g (440 m / 480 yards) of DK-weight yarn

items.name: Colour B (contrast)
items.qty: About 200 g (440 m / 480 yards) of DK-weight yarn in a contrasting value

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4.5 mm (UK 7 / US 7) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

20 stitches and 30 rows to 10 cm over two-colour brioche on 4.5 mm needles, relaxed. Do not wet-block the gauge swatch. Each RS pass adds approximately 5 mm of depth at gauge; at 130 passes the shawl depth reaches approximately 65 cm. The wingspan at 20 stitches per 10 cm with 280 stitches at the cast-off row is approximately 140 cm.
Stitches used

items.name: brk
items.qty: brioche knit: k stitch + its yo together

content.text: Pattern
Garter tab
Work the garter tab in colour A: 3 sts on waste yarn, 6 garter rows, pick up 9 sts. Place spine marker at the centre stitch (stitch 5). All garter-tab rows are in colour A.
Set-up row
Set-up row (colour A): k1, yo, k to spine marker, SM, k1, yo, k to last st, yo, k1. (Yarn-overs added on each side of the spine for the first brioche pass.)
Brioche body
Pass 1 (colour B, RS):
sl1yo
brk
, sl1yo; repeat from * to spine, SM, sl1yo, *brk, sl1yo; repeat from * to last st, brk.
Pass 2 (colour A, WS): brk, *sl1yo, brk; repeat from * to spine marker, SM, brk, *sl1yo, brk; repeat from * to end.
Increase pass (colour A, RS): brk, yo, *sl1yo, brk; repeat from * to spine, SM, k1 (spine in garter), SM, *brk, sl1yo; repeat from * to last 2 sts, yo, brk. (2 new stitches added per increase pass)
Work an increase pass every 6th pass to add width gradually. Continue until wingspan reaches 140 cm.
Bind off
Standard brioche bind-off in colour A: work each brk as a normal k before binding off, each sl1yo as a normal k2tog before binding off. Work loosely.
Common faults

Brioche stitch dropped at increase position: a yarn-over used for the increase was mistaken for a brioche paired yo. Increase yarn-overs sit at the edge; paired brioche yo sit in the body. Mark the increase yo with a removable stitch marker in a different colour.

Both colours worked on the same pass: the colour alternation was lost. Each pass must use only one colour. If both colours are at the same end of the needle, a colour was worked twice in a row. Tink back to the last pass where the colours were correctly separated.
Care
Hand wash gently in cool water. Roll in a towel to remove excess water; lay flat to dry. Do not pin or stretch the brioche fabric.
What to try next
Try a three-colour brioche triangle with colour A as the MC spine garter, and two alternating contrast colours for the two brioche passes.
